gates.reason: '--gate passed is refused unless the run's convergence verdict is verified against the cloud store' is real (ship-commit.mjs enforces it — observed live this session), but its exit code depends on the git + .audit/last-audit-run.json evidence state (exit 1 vs 2 across setups), so a hermetic cli-exit fixture cannot bind it DETERMINISTICALLY — the trigger state is subtle and store-dependent. The refusal itself is verified by ship-commit's own provenance tests; document-only here rather than a fragile recipe.

'Do NOT git add <Category-A artifact>' (scripts/.sync-manifest.json, dashboard/index.html, dashboard/telemetry.html, docs/architecture-map.md) is an instruction to the AGENT running /ship about what NOT to stage. Still document-only as a GATE — there is no ship-CLI exit code to assert, because the rule constrains what the model chooses to stage, not what a command returns. REVISED 2026-07-26: the previous reason claimed this was 'enforced downstream by .gitignore, not by a ship CLI' and stopped there, which read as 'not mechanically checkable' and was wrong — the SKILL TEXT side is now guarded by tests/skill-staging-instructions.test.mjs, which fails when any shell-fenced `git add <literal path>` line in skills/** names a gitignored path. That guard exists because prose alone failed twice: dashboard/index.html (2026-06) got a 'do NOT stage' note, and docs/architecture-map.md then kept its `git add` line for six days sitting two steps above that very note until an agent followed it on 2026-07-26.

'Step 0.5 pre-ship gates are non-blocking by default; a query failure never makes the gate stricter OR blind' is a NEGATIVE guarantee about the agent's orchestration of the pre-ship queries. Asserting an absence-of-blocking across cloud-off / query-failure / no-session states is a judgement about agent flow, not a single CLI exit; document-only.
